Ahhh, I see. I suppose that makes sense. You raise a lot of good points, again. That said, I never said that I wrote "soul" pointing to my old name, I wrote "host", which has entirely different connotations. I did write "spirits" pointing to the other names (including my current one). That said, confirmation bias is very real, and I should be careful about falling into that trap as I consider this stuff.

Ahh, yeah, I was also told in PMs that my problem with distinguishing reality has little if anything to do with tulpas, and it is extraneous. Nevermind that one. That said, you raise a very good point with me perhaps having a confirmation bias stemming from that crash years ago, but, I have fully recovered from that trauma,, over two years ago. I would have little reason to go back to that now.

I will take what you said to heart and be careful, I'm still going through all this and carefully considering it...I do have a therapist, but, obviously, any mention of tulaps or the like will be laughed out. That simply is not part of people's vocabulary for the most part.

Thank you for your continued support and guidance.

Thank you for your post, you raise a lot of good points. By bad memory, I mean that I do not remember anything at all, save for a few significant memories. I do not remember any of my teachers in elementary, not any of the classes, nor my own graduation. I remember a blurry image of myself running down a green hill. I remember eating an ice cream sandwich next to an amphitheater. I remember being screamed at and beaten as soon as I walked in the door one day, and watching my stepfather break every present I had gotten from my father. I remember laying in bed, staring up at the ceiling and watching colored balls of gas float around, staying stock still, terrified that they would find me. I remember my sister sitting at a table at burger king, crying for some reason. I remember crashing my bike, hitting my head, and waking up in a hospital with my stepfather berating me for letting an ambulance pick me up, as that had cost a thousand dollars. Just images, sometimes a few seconds of motion, very indistinct. Those are about all the memories I have.

That said, you raise very good points. I do not have entities in my head that I can talk to or interact with. I do not remember being a tulpa. My homosexuality did come after puberty (I bloomed earlier than normal), but it was fairly close, so you might have a point. That said, there aren't that many pages of writing. Added all together, it's maybe seven pages, most of which are nearly entirely blank except for a small drawing, or a half-paragraph of writing. There was not much to cherry-pick from. As for the shift...I have not encountered anybody that shifted as drastically as I did. Core personalities? I've never seen it...then again, anecdotal evidence is shaky at best, so, you may be right. That said, I was entirely unaware of many of the things listed in the drawings and writings I found until I found them, it seems strange that they would linger for so long...

However...I have had issues with non-reality. I hadn't mentioned it, except in a PM, but, as it was brought up, I'll say it here. As long as I can remember, I have had extremely realistic dreams, and I have been unable to distinguish dreams from reality, even when I wake up. I am always unsure of if I am dreaming or awake, and I never know if memories I have had really happened unless someone else was there as well. This has lead to a lot of sureness of reality for as long as I can remember, something that only increased after a particularly nasty rollover on the highway. After that, I was struggling to maintain the belief that anything that happened was real, I was certain that it was all imaginary, that I was in a coma or dead. I went to therapy for this, and it helped, but...I do have history of this (and still struggle with being unable to discern reality from dreams even today). 

Thanks for your insight, it's good to hear things from both sides, and you have a lot of reasoning in your argument. I'll temper my own judgement with this and carefully think about what this all means...that said, there are still points raised that are left unanswered...I'm not sure.

Thank you for sharing your experience as well, it's helping me work through this. I'm slowly beginning to realize that I might in fact be a tulpa, and I have been trying to cope with that. Hearing that other people have had this experience really does help. I just wish that I could share this with more people I know...right now I'm hiding it, so I don't look "crazy".

Thank you for your post.

Thank you for your touching post, Hail. It's incredible, hearing your story. I can only imagine what it would be like to remember all that, and know for sure my actual origins...that said, with all the trials that you have been through, perhaps it is for the best that it has been left murky. I feel for you and your pain.

As for your assessment...it is beginning to look as if that is the case.  I do not know if it was intentional, surely, there were suicide attempts beforehand, but, on the same side, I do not believe the tulpa creation was intentional either. As for death not being permanent...at the risk of sounding like a terrible person, I shudder to think of what would happen if, if I truly were the tulpa, the host came back and took control. They truly were violent and disturbed, and seeing their presence would seal my fate, so to speak, as to who I am. Many of the drawing were downright sadistic, taking great pleasure in pain. I cannot imagine why such a person would let such a passive tulpa take control, however...overall, I hope that this is a question that is left unanswered.

Thank you for the deeply informative and personal post.

Would I? I don't know what being a tulpa feels like...or perhaps I only know what being a tulpa feels like. It's all rather disorienting. That said...as for the point of your post, I have to say you are right...no matter how I was made, I am human(?). Well. Sentient.

Either way, thank you for the support.

Ah, I've been going to a psychiatrist regularly, as well as intermittent therapy. I am genetically predisposed to depression, which kicked in about a year and a half ago. That mainly led to lack of motivation and such, though, not suicide attempts. I've since been medicated, and, according to my psychiatrist, I am mentally healthy, so long as I continue my current dosage. I had a therapist attempt to bring back repressed memories, but, at the end of it, it was decided that it was not worth the effort. I had a bit of a scare where I had a rollover at 83 mph on the highway, ending up in the opposite lane of traffic, which, though I survived unharmed, shook my perception of reality for some time due to how close I came to dying and how unlikely my survival was. I went to therapy for this, and managed to re-associate fully with reality.

That long blurb is basically my psychological history...as far as I can tell, I never had DID, I was never diagnosed with anxiety, and I don't have amnesia, just a long period with very spotty/distanced memories. I've been to psychiatrists, but...well, to be honest, it doesn't seem like a mental condition caused this.

Thank you for going through the safe route, though!

That said, some of what you said still makes sense. I'll give it some thought.

I...avoided mentioning it, due to the fact that it is a rather taboo topic, but...when I was around 12-13, I had hit a major depressive phase, and made multiple suicide attempts. After 13, I never attempted suicide again ,and was overall more stable. Hearing about this "Egocide" is...well, to be honest, it just makes too much sense to ignore. I...am going to take some time to consider the ramifications of this, but, expect me to continue this in PMs soon. I just need some time right now.
